_: EP 10 — Zomato's New Year's Eve. Visual register comes from references/ep10-inspo/ (a WhatsApp brand still, pinned by unbserved): cream field #F7F4EF, every shape carrying a ~3px #1C1C1C stroke, rounded cards tumbling at angles across a single-hue ramp, gold stars as punctuation, the brand mark large and centred and still. Zomato's Cranberry #E23744 is exact — it is the fill in their own wordmark SVG. Display face is Metropolis, the open-source base of Zomato's Okra, so this is the real typeface rather than a lookalike. The director chose to keep full photoreal footage against this flat register after being warned the two fight; the reconciliation is that every Kling clip is framed INSIDE an outlined rounded card, so the stroke language runs through both registers instead of the two sitting side by side. Numbers: references/ep10-facts.md, sourced only.
title: India orders dinner at midnight. All of it, at once.
subtitle: Four hundred fifty million messages a minute, eleven thousand servers, and fifteen days of rehearsal
_voice: Same voice as EP09 — series continuity. But NOT eleven_v3 this time. The director asked for a directive read with no modulation, so the model is eleven_multilingual_v2, which CANNOT perform audio tags at all: tts.mjs refuses to record a tagged line on a non-v3 model, which makes 'no modulation' a structural guarantee rather than a setting that drifts. v2 also gets previous_text/next_text continuity that v3 lacks, so one steady register holds across all eighteen lines. Stability high, style near zero. The authority comes from the writing — imperatives, front-loaded subjects, full stops where a weaker script would use commas.
_vo: 18 beats, ~2:30. ZERO audio tags by design — see _voice. Every figure is spelled out as words, never digits, because that is where a synthetic mouth most reliably embarrasses you. Contractions throughout. The three chapter slates are structure, not performance: short and flat.

vo.text: Eleven fifty-eight at night. In two minutes, the biggest food delivery night in India begins.
This is what it takes to survive it… every single year.
Most systems scale for a curve. Zomato scales for a CLIFF… one that arrives on schedule.
A kitchen has a hard ceiling. So does a connection pool… Tonight, both of them find it.
Order volume does not rise on New Year's Eve. It STEPS… and it stays stepped for hours.
So nothing waits on anything. Every action becomes a message. The queue is the architecture.
That night, Kafka carried four hundred and fifty million messages a minute… Five point six gigabytes per second.
You cannot fix what you cannot see. Their logging platform swallowed sixty terabytes in a single day.
Two point two billion active time series. Seventeen point eight million data points every second.
The night is won… in December.
Fifteen days of load testing. Thirty billion requests fired at their own systems… deliberately.
Eleven thousand instances, pre-scaled before anyone ordered. Autoscaling is too slow when the step is vertical.
Then they break it themselves… Inject the failure while the audience is still nobody.
Three million orders… Sixty percent of them delivered in under thirty minutes.

You cannot load-test appetite. Every year the model is wrong… Every year, they rebuild it.

Follow for more.

_shots: 12 text-to-video jobs through the Kling MCP, plus 3 image-to-video morph bridges added after the first render pass (they need real stills from the scenes either side). The MCP exposes no 'negative' parameter — unlike the direct API path in kling.mjs — so every exclusion is written into the prompt tail instead. Two visual families only: WARM (street, kitchen, crowd, dawn — amber and red, shallow, alive) and COLD (ops room, data centre — blue-grey, wide, still). The cut between those two families IS the argument of the episode. Kling never renders text, signage, UI or numbers: every legible thing in this film is Remotion.
